messages.author: dd07ff0ed5d277f7
messages.subject: Combining different groups into one
parts:
Hello,

I tried to map 100 markers from the same chromosome. After forming linkage groups, these were mapped to 4 different groups (though no problematic markers ). Can you please tell me how to bring them into one group.

Thanks

messages.author: 96353e7106735838
messages.subject: Re: [Rqtl-disc] Combining different groups into one
parts:
You can try using the function movemarker() to move markers from one linkage group to another.

For example, with the hyper dataset, to paste all of the markers on chromosome 12 onto the end of chromosome 11, you could do:

data(hyper)
c12markers <- markernames(hyper, chr=12)
for(marker in c12markers) {
hyper <- movemarker(hyper, marker, 11)
}

karl

Thanks Karl,

The function movemarker() works when we use the input file with markers from more two or more chr (say chr=11 and 12). 

I used the input file with 100 markers which belong to one chr (say chr=1). After mapping, these are falling into 3 groups after > lg <- formLinkageGroups(mapthis, max.rf=0.35, min.lod=6) function. Though I tried different rf and lod values,  I am getting same 3 groups. Based on the physical location, I expect all 100 markers to be placed in one group. Please suggest how to do it.

Thanks

messages.author: 96353e7106735838
messages.subject: Re: [Rqtl-disc] Combining different groups into one
parts:
Try reducing min.lod and increasing max.rf.

The main thing I'd focus on is figuring out why the markers are breaking up into three groups. To start, I'd look at tables of two-locus genotypes for marker pairs that are close by physically but are getting put into different linkage groups. Also I'd look at the plot.rf() image, with markers ordered by their physical location.

karl
